findings.quote: but rather what it befits themselves to do—so too with abuse
findings.problem: The Greek breaks off at 'τοῦτο μᾶλλον *' and resumes after a gap at '** οὕτως καὶ περὶ τῶν λοιδοριῶν'. The English runs the two halves together as one whole sentence, silently smoothing the lacuna.
findings.proposed_fix: but rather what it befits themselves to do, this more [...] [text lost] ... so too with abuse

findings.quote: even if some such disgrace had truly attached to Demochares
findings.proposed_fix: even if some such misfortune had truly attached to Demochares

units.note: Chapter opens mid-word (κει) in the Greek; English 'anything of the kind' is acceptable.

findings.quote: not realizing that falsehood is no less present in those who in their histories pass over in silence what actually happened than in those who misstate it
findings.problem: Greek has a lacuna: 'τοὺς τὰ γεγονότα *** γράφοντας ἐν ταῖς ἱστορίαις' (falsehood is no less found among those who write the events [gap] in their histories). The English invents a complete contrast (silence vs misstatement) that the surviving Greek does not give.
findings.proposed_fix: not realizing that falsehood is no less found among those who write what happened [text lost] in their histories

findings.quote: offering his backside to the front of all who wished
findings.problem: 'πάντων τῶν βουλομένων τοῖς ὄπισθεν ἔμπροσθεν γεγονότα': he became, for all who wished, 'front' to their 'behind' (his front put in the place of the rear). The English reverses who offers what and garbles the reversal-of-front-and-back point.
findings.proposed_fix: having made his front a rear for all who wished

units.note: Obscene idiom; the Greek is ambiguous in detail, preserve the front/back reversal.
Section heading 'V. De Callisthenis Imperitia...' in the Greek is an editor's rubric, omitted in English; not an error.
'front ... depth' for πλάτος/μῆκος is interpretive but not wrong in sense.

Greek is corrupt/fragmentary at 'λείπειν τῶν δεκατεττάρων σταδίων *' and between the lacunae; the English marks the gaps (* ** [...]) and its rendering 'fell short of fourteen stades' is a literal reading of an unclear clause. Verbs 'was taken up' and 'had to stand' are supplied by the translator; the construction is elliptical in Greek. No fix proposed.
